app.title: CD40 Immunosome: signalling ODE simulator with knockout synergy and robustness checks
app.summary: The person sets the rate constants and input level of a small feedback signalling model with sidebar sliders, and picks a delivery vehicle and an agonist. They then switch between modules. One draws the pathway as a network with the current rates on its edges. One plots the simulated time courses with steady-state sweeps over two parameters. One scores simulated gene knockouts by how much each changes the area under the response curve. One checks the model against a no-feedback null and against Monte Carlo jitter of all parameters. At the end they download a plain-text summary of the setup, the equations and the scoring formula.

task.text: Explore how a feedback signalling model responds to its parameters and to simulated knockouts, and check that its behaviour holds under perturbation, to generate hypotheses for the lab.

data.text: Simulated time courses from a small system of ordinary differential equations. The data is generated from sliders for the rate constants, plus small built-in tables of knockout effects, delivery-vehicle properties and candidate proteins.
data.item: one simulated run of the signalling model under a given set of rate constants

stage.text: analysing a mechanistic signalling model and testing its robustness, before wet-lab validation

mechanism.text: Sidebar sliders and selectors hold one shared parameter set. Each module re-simulates from it and redraws its own charts: a network diagram, time-course and sweep line charts, a sorted bar chart and table of knockout scores, and envelope and histogram charts from a seeded Monte Carlo run. A download button writes out the current setup as text.

field.text: ODE kinetic modelling of a signalling pathway in systems immunology

workflow.name: tune a mechanistic model and score perturbations against its baseline

steps.here: Sliders set seven rate constants and the receptor input level; selectors choose the delivery vehicle and the agonist. Every module reads these values.
The pathway is drawn as a physics-laid-out network with rate constants on the edges. Beside it are metrics for the vehicle's clustering regime, its presentation gain, and a damping ratio.

steps.step: compute a value from the data
steps.here: The equations are integrated with RK4 to plot the three species over time. The steady state is reported, k1 and k4 are each swept over 15 values, and the result is compared with the linear analytical steady state.

Each simulated knockout scales its rate constants. Its response AUC and time-to-peak are compared with the baseline, the knockouts are ranked by synergy score in a bar chart and a table, and one is picked to read its mechanistic note.

steps.step: check the result holds under perturbation
steps.here: The model is plotted against a null with no feedback. A seeded button runs 50 simulations with every parameter jittered by ±20%, showing a mean ±1σ envelope, optional raw trajectories, peak and time-to-peak statistics, and an AUC histogram.
A button downloads a TXT summary of the chosen vehicle and agonist, the constants, the equations and the synergy formula.

distinctive: There is no imported data: every view is regenerated from the sidebar's rate constants by integrating a coupled ODE system with a hand-written RK4 solver.
Perturbations are scored by the percentage change in area under the curve against baseline, alongside the shift in time-to-peak.
Robustness is tested two ways: against a null model with the feedback loop switched off, and by seeded Monte Carlo jitter of all parameters.
The simulated steady state is checked against a closed-form linear approximation, with the percent deviation and a convergence check reported.
